purpose: Dalbavancin is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial skin infections, including infections that cause redness, swelling, and warmth. It works against some tough bacteria, including MRSA, which is a type of staph bacteria that resists many common antibiotics. Your doctor may choose this medicine when a strong, long-lasting antibiotic is needed.
how_it_works: Dalbavancin works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria, essentially breaking down the protective barrier the bacteria need to survive. Without this wall, the bacteria fall apart and die. Because it sticks around in your body for a long time, it can keep fighting the infection with just one or two doses instead of daily pills.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, headache, and diarrhea. Some people notice redness, itching, or a rash, especially if the medicine is given too quickly through the IV. You might also have mild constipation or vomiting.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to any antibiotics, especially vancomycin or other glycopeptide antibiotics, as you could have a serious allergic reaction. If you develop a severe rash, hives, difficulty breathing, or flushing during or after the infusion, get medical help right away. Also let your doctor know if you have liver problems, since this medicine is processed by the liver. Like all antibiotics, using dalbavancin when you do not need it can make it less effective over time.
typical_dosing: Dalbavancin is given as an IV infusion directly into a vein by a nurse or doctor, so you do not take it as a pill at home. The most common schedule is either one single dose or two doses given one week apart. Each infusion is given slowly over 30 minutes. Because it stays in your body for a long time, this short treatment schedule is often all that is needed.
